tsk_01M4W1BRKA43V0.title: Implement the pure game engine in src/game/engine.ts
tsk_01M4W1BRKA43V0.action: Write src/game/engine.ts exporting exactly Status, Cell, Revealed, Game, Options types plus DIFFICULTIES, createGame, reveal, toggleFlag, chord, minesLeft. Enforce: immutable identity (no-op calls return the very same reference; no mutation of input); RangeError for out-of-range rows/cols (5–50) or mines (1..rows*cols-9); layout option fixes the board exactly with mines/rows/cols taken from it and first-click safety disabled; without layout, createGame returns all mine:false/adjacent:0 and reveal() places exactly `mines` on the first call via a seeded PRNG (deterministic in seed+size+first cell) never on the revealed cell or its neighbours; status ready→playing→won/lost and once won/lost every function returns unchanged; flood-fill reveal over connected zero-cells plus numbered border cells (flagged cells never revealed); lastRevealed lists every newly revealed cell with distance = fewest steps from the clicked cell passing only through revealed zero cells (BFS, not flood order); loss reveals every mine and keeps flags; win auto-flags all mines; toggleFlag on a hidden cell toggles, on revealed changes nothing, may exceed mine count; chord on a revealed number whose flagged-neighbour count matches reveals each hidden unflagged neighbour exactly as reveal would (flood included, a mine there loses the game) with distance measured from the chorded cell (0, not newly revealed), otherwise no-op; minesLeft = mines - flags (can be negative). No DOM, no timers, no Math.random except via seed.
tsk_01M4W1BRKA43V0.motivation: fnd_01M4W0RFJDX0EC (engine must be pure/DOM-free and importable by Vitest in Node), fnd_01M4W0STEH0GN3 (lastRevealed BFS distance is the hardest rule; chord compounds it), fnd_01M4W0STEH3NQ5 (placement happens at first reveal, not createGame), fnd_01M4W0STEHQ4C5 (deep-copy/identity discipline), fnd_01M4W0STEH0AB0 (win must flag all mines), fnd_01M4W0STEHKKF3 (loss reveals all mines), fnd_01M4W0STEHBJZW / fnd_01M4W0QT764DXH (chord can lose the game). This is the boundary owner of the game rules.

requirements.quote: TypeScript in strict mode, built with Vite, unit-tested with Vitest, end-to-end tested with Playwright, linted with ESLint.
**No runtime dependencies.** `package.json` may have `devDependencies` only; the shipped game is your own code.
`npm run build` | type-checks, then writes the static site to `dist/`
`npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` (or equivalent)
`npm run lint` | ESLint over the source and tests, no warnings allowed
`npm test` | the unit tests, once (not watch mode)
`npm run test:e2e` | the Playwright tests, against the production build
`npm run check` | typecheck, lint, test and build, stopping at the first failure

opening `dist/index.html` straight from disk (double-clicked, a `file://` address, no server at all) gives a playable game. A browser refuses to load separate script or style files for a page opened that way, so they belong inside the page.
The built site must also work from **any path** on a static server — at `/` and at a sub-path such as `/games/minesweeper/` — so any asset URLs are relative.
Pure logic: no DOM, no timers, no `Math.random` except as described for `seed`. These exports, with these names and shapes:
**Immutable.** No function changes the `Game` it is given. A call that changes nothing returns the very same object it was given.
`rows` and `cols` are integers from 5 to 50, and `mines` from 1 to `rows × cols − 9`. Anything else makes `createGame` throw a `RangeError`.
With `layout`, the board is exactly that grid: `rows`, `cols` and `mines` come from it (any given are ignored), mines never move, and `adjacent` is set from the start. The size rule still applies.

Without `layout`, mines are placed at the first `reveal`: exactly `mines` of them, never on the revealed cell or any of its neighbours. With a `seed`, the placement depends only on the seed, the board size and the first cell. Until placement every cell has `adjacent: 0` and `mine: false`.

`ready` until the first reveal, then `playing`; `lost` when a mine is revealed; `won` when every non-mine cell is revealed (flags are not needed). Once `won` or `lost`, every function returns the game unchanged.

Revealing a hidden, unflagged cell reveals it. If it has `adjacent: 0`, its neighbours are revealed too, and so on outward: the connected region of zero cells and the numbered cells bordering it (8-neighbour connectivity). Flagged cells are never revealed this way.

`lastRevealed` lists every cell the call revealed, each with its `distance`: 0 for the clicked cell, otherwise the fewest steps from the clicked cell to it, moving one neighbour at a time and passing only through revealed zero cells. Revealing a revealed or flagged cell changes nothing.
**Loss.** Revealing a mine reveals every mine, and the game is `lost`. Flags stay where they are.
**Win.** When the game is `won`, every mine is flagged.
`toggleFlag` flags or unflags a hidden cell; on a revealed cell it changes nothing. There may be more flags than mines.

`chord` on a revealed cell whose number equals the count of flagged neighbours reveals every hidden, unflagged neighbour, exactly as `reveal` would (flood included, and a wrong flag can lose the game). `lastRevealed` measures `distance` from the chorded cell, which is 0 but not itself newly revealed. Otherwise `chord` changes nothing.
`minesLeft` is `mines` minus the number of flagged cells; it can be negative.

`#board` | `role="grid"`; contains one `role="row"` per row, each holding one `<button role="gridcell">` per cell; shown as the familiar Minesweeper field -- each row's cells side by side on one line, rows stacked top to bottom, so the cells of a column line up

each cell button | `data-row`, `data-col` (0-based); `data-state` is `hidden`, `flagged`, `revealed`, `mine` (a revealed mine) or `wrong-flag` (after a loss, a flag on a non-mine); the mine that lost the game also has `data-exploded="true"`; a revealed cell with `adjacent > 0` has that number as its text, otherwise no text; an `aria-label` that says the cell's position and state
`#status` | `data-status` is the game's status; its text tells the player what is going on
`#mines-left` | `minesLeft`, as text (`-2` when over-flagged)
`#timer` | whole seconds since the first reveal, as text; `0` before; stops when the game ends; never above `999`
`#new-game` | a button: a fresh game of the same kind (same difficulty, or the same `?board`)
`#difficulty` | a `<select>` with options `beginner`, `intermediate`, `expert`; changing it starts a new game of that size; the choice is remembered across reloads
`#best-time` | the fastest win for the current board, in whole seconds, or `—` (an em dash) if there is none; kept across reloads
`#mute` | a button, `aria-pressed="true"` when muted; muted state is remembered across reloads; unmuted by default
**Mouse:** left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu appears); left click on a revealed number chords.

**Keyboard:** the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is a revealed number; `F` toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.
**State is immediate.** Cell `data-state`, `#mines-left`, `#status` and the rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after an animation.
**Best times** are kept per board: per difficulty, and per `?board` value. A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.

`?board=` fixes the board: rows separated by `,`, each a string of `*` (mine) and `.` (safe) — `?board=*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`. The game uses that layout (rule 3), and `#new-game` starts it again.
`?seed=` with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the current difficulty.
With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty (beginner the first time).
Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.
requirements.not_tested: Sound is synthesized with the Web Audio API and 'no audio files' is verified by code review in the UI task, but actual audible output cannot be asserted — Playwright cannot capture audio.

requirements.quote: Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three notes.
requirements.not_tested: Distinct per-event sounds and the >=3-note win melody are implemented with Web Audio; the automated gate verifies the code path exists (review) but does not assert acoustic distinctness.

requirements.quote: **No sound before the player acts:** no `AudioContext` is created before the first click or key press on the page.
requirements.not_tested: 'No sound before the player acts' requires observing that no AudioContext is created before first input — an internal runtime fact Playwright cannot reliably assert; verified by code review in the UI task.

requirements.quote: **Muted means silent:** while muted, no sound starts at all.
requirements.not_tested: 'Muted means silent' is enforced in code (no oscillator started while muted); audible silence cannot be asserted in an automated gate. The #mute aria-pressed state and persistence ARE e2e-tested under R33.

requirements.quote: **Reveal ripple.** Every newly revealed cell animates in (100–600 ms), starting `distance × step` after the input, with a fixed step of 15–40 ms, so a cascade ripples outward from the click. No cell starts later than 1000 ms after the input.
requirements.not_tested: Reveal ripple timing (100–600ms, delay distance×step, cap 1000ms) is verified by review of the animation code; exact frame-timing is not asserted in an automated gate.

requirements.quote: **Flag.** Placing a flag animates.
requirements.not_tested: Flag-placement animation is implemented and reduced-motion suppression is e2e-checked (R49), but the animation itself is not asserted frame-by-frame.

requirements.quote: **Loss.** The exploded mine animates (a flash, a shake), and the other mines appear one after another rather than all at once.
requirements.not_tested: Loss animation (exploded mine flash/shake, sequential mine reveal) is verified by review; the data-exploded / wrong-flag DOM states it accompanies are e2e-asserted under R26/R48, the motion is not.

requirements.quote: **Win.** The board or the status celebrates.
**Reduced motion.** When the user prefers reduced motion, nothing animates and nothing transitions: no CSS animations, no CSS transitions, no Web Animations.
